title: Timing-sensitive durable gates under host load (not a regression)
subtitle: Same rig, alternating trees back to back; colima VM 2 vCPU on a host at load 57-97; DurableLocalRuntimeFaultGateTest (10 cases) per run

blocks.label: adoptedWorkerCanCancelItsOriginalActiveCall only, DISPATCH_LEASE 2 s (rig) vs 10 s (copy)
blocks.pre:
== 2 s  : 2/2, 1/2, 2/2   ('cancellation must reach the original active worker ==> expected: <1> but was: <0>')
++ 10 s : 2/2, 2/2, 2/2
== full Stage F on the round-3 head: 38/39, then 33/39 (ConcurrencyStorage… x2, closingAnObserver… x2, adoptedWorkerCanCancel… x2)
++ isolated reruns of the ConcurrencyStorage gate: head 3/3, base 2d95f1aed8 3/3; landing tree full Stage F 39/39

blocks.note: The gate assumes the restarted Broker is up and cancels inside the 2 s dispatch lease. On a slow host the dispatch lapses first, and the existing contract then fences it, so no transport cancel is sent. Both heads fail the same way, and a 10 s lease removed the failures in this small sample. These gates don't run in CI; widening the lease for this gate would keep it meaningful as a release gate.
